title: Sable and the Extraction
premise: Silas Delacroix spent a decade laundering his past into respectability as a financial-crimes investigator, hiding the years he spent as an off-books asset for a covert network called the Meridian Group. When a woman named Ada Voss repays a favor he has no memory of doing—pulling him out of a burning safehouse in Prague, a night his mind has erased—she demands the debt be settled by helping her extract her brother, a Meridian accountant who knows where the bodies and the billions are buried. As Silas investigates his own missing night, he discovers the Group deliberately wiped his memory to bury evidence of a massacre, and that his handler, the man he still loves like a brother, ordered it. To save Ada's brother and himself, Silas must reconstruct the erased night, burn Meridian's financial skeleton from the inside, and choose between the polished lie of his old loyalty and the dangerous truth. In the end, Silas trades his own clean escape to detonate the network's ledger publicly, walks away with Ada and a memory he finally owns, and lets the man who betrayed him face the consequences instead of the bullet.
about_author: Sable Reyes is a former compliance analyst who spent eight years tracing shell companies across three continents before trading the spreadsheet for the manuscript. She writes thrillers about people whose clean lives are built on dirty foundations, and she still keeps a go-bag packed out of habit.

chapters.title: The Polished Lie
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. We meet him mid-ritual: morning run, packed go-bag in the closet, a flawless investigator's life built over a buried past. He flags a suspicious account at work and is quietly ordered to drop it. The beat is controlled dread—the reader sees the seams before he admits they exist.

chapters.title: A Debt Never Owed
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Ada Voss appears at his office with a photograph of a Prague safehouse fire and says, 'You pulled me out. I'm here to repay it.' Silas has no memory of Prague. The beat is vertigo—a stranger holding a version of him he doesn't recognize.

chapters.title: Interest Accrued
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Over a diner coffee, she lays out her ask: extract her brother Tomas, a Meridian accountant, before the Group silences him. Silas refuses, but she leaves the photograph. The beat is reluctant gravity—he studies the photo and feels his body remember fear his mind cannot.

chapters.title: The Handler
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. He calls Marcus Hale, his old handler and closest friend, to ask about Prague. Marcus is warm, deflecting, and lies smoothly—too smoothly. That night Silas finds a Meridian cipher in his own handwriting that he doesn't remember writing. The beat is betrayal's first cold touch.

chapters.title: Ledger of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Using investigator tools on himself, he traces money from the Prague fire to a shell company he once controlled. Someone has been maintaining his cover for years—paying rent on his amnesia. The beat is horror reframed as accounting.

chapters.title: Tomas
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV, intercepted. In a Lisbon safe flat, Tomas copies Meridian's master ledger onto two drives and mails one to Ada. He knows the clock is running. The beat is desperate competence—a small man racing a large machine.

chapters.title: The Wipe
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A hypnotist-adjacent neurologist confirms his memory gap is chemically induced, professionally. Meridian erases people, and Silas was one. The beat is grief for a self he can't retrieve—and the first flicker of resolve.

chapters.title: Clean Money, Dirty Hands
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada and Silas map Meridian's financial skeleton from her brother's partial data. Working together, their friction turns to trust, then something warmer. The beat is intimacy built on shared danger.

chapters.title: What Marcus Knew
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas confronts Marcus at a charity gala, probing under the small talk. Marcus warns him off with genuine fear in his eyes—and Silas realizes Marcus is afraid of someone above him. The beat is love and suspicion sharing a glass of wine.

chapters.title: Lisbon Falling
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Meridian's cleaners reach Lisbon; Tomas runs, drive in hand, and goes dark after a near-miss on the tram line. The beat is breathless pursuit and the cost of knowing too much.

chapters.title: Extraction Point
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada and Silas fly to Lisbon to intercept Tomas before Meridian does. Silas's old tradecraft resurfaces—muscle memory the wipe couldn't reach. The beat is the past arming the present.

chapters.title: The Night He Lost
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A Meridian archive in Lisbon holds footage of the Prague fire: Silas did pull Ada out—but he also watched Meridian execute six witnesses, and he carried the order out himself. His memory was wiped to protect him from his own complicity. The beat is devastation; the hero learns he was also the weapon.

chapters.title: Reunion, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. They find Tomas in a dockside chapel; Meridian's cleaners arrive minutes behind them. A brutal escape through the port leaves Silas shot and Tomas's second drive destroyed. The beat is sacrifice and narrowing odds.

chapters.title: Blood and Interest
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Recovering in a safehouse, Silas and Ada admit what's growing between them, and Silas confesses the Prague footage. Ada's forgiveness is conditional: he helps her burn Meridian completely. The beat is love choosing truth over comfort.

chapters.title: The Man Above Marcus
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Following the money upward, Silas identifies Director Corvane, the architect of the wipe program—and discovers Marcus is scheduled to be Meridian's next erased asset, the fall guy for everything. The beat is the trap closing on the man who lied to protect him.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus meets Silas off the books, finally honest: he ordered the wipe to save Silas's life, trading his own soul for it. He gives Silas Corvane's schedule and asks for nothing. The beat is forgiveness extended and not yet accepted.

chapters.title: The Ledger Bomb
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The team plans the endgame: inject Tomas's master ledger into every regulator, journalist, and Meridian account simultaneously, then extract Tomas out of Geneva. The beat is cold, careful hope—plan the miracle, expect the massacre.

chapters.title: Geneva, Hour Zero
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The operation begins: Tomas inside Meridian's Geneva server vault, Ada on overwatch, Silas walking through the front door wearing his old cover. Corvane is waiting for him. The beat is a wolf returning to the den on purpose.

chapters.title: Everything Owed
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Confrontation with Corvane, who offers Silas his wiped life back—clean, painless, restored. Silas refuses, triggers the ledger release, and fights his way out as Meridian's empire begins collapsing in real time. The beat is the climax: truth as detonation.

chapters.title: The Bullet He Doesn't Fire
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Cornered by Corvane's remaining cleaners, Marcus is saved when Silas arrives—not to save the network, but the man. Silas lets the law take Corvane alive rather than execute him. The beat is loyalty redefined: not obedience, but refusal to become the weapon.

chapters.title: After the Fire
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Meridian's leaders are arrested as the ledger goes global; Tomas testifies. Ada and Silas, both burned and both free, decide what a life without the network looks like. The beat is tender exhaustion—love that survived the truth.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag, Unpacked
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Months later, Silas unpacks the go-bag for good, keeps one Prague photograph on the shelf, and visits Marcus in prison—forgiveness, slowly. He remembers the night he lost, and keeps it. The beat is resolution: memory owned, duty answered, love chosen.
